findings.topic: API, persisted values and export preservation
findings.detail: AST extraction finds unchanged five workflow API call expressions/order. Member GET uses the initiating immutable batch ID captured as batchId and validated against the returned snapshot. Past-duty history GET moves to scoped helper with captured id. Other nine past-duty API expressions—including inspect, preview, apply file/options/hash, policy save, template and rejected CSV—remain exact. No new mutation endpoint, storage write, auth/header code, server query term, filename or CSV transformation introduced. See complete extracted calls; member/past textual argument changes are expressly not claimed byte-identical.

Helper trims/lowercases/splits whitespace and performs AND matching via includes over supplied displayed strings. No regex construction, eval, selector/query interpolation or HTML sink. Search values assigned with value; new counts, filtered-detail notices and errors use textContent. Existing dynamic filenames/accounts/IDs/string outcomes and JSON displays continue escaped. IDs/raw hidden fields do not participate in matching.

findings.topic: Member ID mismatch, failure and recovery
findings.detail: batchId is captured before awaiting and requestedBatch must exist in history. Returned batch.batch.id mismatch throws before painting details; catch names the requested filename/ID and exposes explicit GET retry. Previous successful detail remains independently named. Detail sequence and host generation/connectivity gates protect painting, control restoration and focus after remount/detach. The entire returned-list snapshot and row IDs remain unmodified; filtering toggles hidden on existing rows.

findings.topic: Workflow ownership, IDs and download errors
findings.detail: Delegated handlers and render/list updates check connected host/current generation. Search shell persists during action rendering; selected immutable ID and original paging arithmetic survive zero-match search. New outside-results notice uses textContent. Initial failure retries only existing history GET. Download still invokes unchanged authenticated helper, whose non-OK/empty-body/session-generation failures occur before blob URL creation; action catch surfaces message and finally releases busy state. Readonly requests are not aborted; an already requested download can finish after unmount if its session remains current. Workflow row response schema has no batch ID, so it cannot independently validate a returned ID; association relies on captured request ID/URL.

findings.topic: Past-duty native busy gate and draft preservation
findings.detail: History GET sets original busy/activeAction history, disables existing fieldsets and original refresh/history actions without rebuilding upload/preview nodes. It snapshots each fieldset/button disabled state and restores only connected current-owner nodes; replacement filtered row buttons recover original ID state or baseline non-busy default. isCurrent/request guards protect detail writes and restoration; retainActionFocus cleanup is always called with currentness. Search/clear update only history list/count; search change returns before existing upload invalidation. Upload File/options/approval/save branches remain unchanged in the genuine diff.

findings.topic: Past-duty retry and retained detail association
findings.detail: Failure names selected immutable ID, keeps prior detail under its own Loaded batch label, and explicit retry calls loadHistoryRows(selectedHistoryId) only. No Apply replay or automatic retry introduced. Past-duty detail schema has no batch ID; no invented returned-ID assurance is claimed.

findings.topic: Malformed numeric fields and transport validation
findings.detail: All three genuine baselines already interpolate typed numeric count/row values directly into HTML. This wave retains that trust assumption; TypeScript does not validate runtime JSON. Deliberately malformed numeric-schema data and globally validated response schemas remain outside this pass. Past-duty workbook template path still omits spreadsheet-signature flag in existing transport; no XLSX parser/signature hardening claim made. These are existing bounded follow-ups, not demonstrated exploit/new regression.
